summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn continued the series on Psalm 23 with part six, focusing on verse 5: "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows." He opened by encouraging anyone in a hard season with Paul's words that we can be pressed but not crushed, and he reminded the church that God can use our hardest places to help others. Pastor Travis explained that in verse 5 the scene shifts from the valley of verse 4 to a banquet, with the shepherd now acting as a host. Rather than only asking God to remove every enemy, David shows God providing for him right in front of them. Pastor Travis described enemies as anything or anyone that opposes us or our God-given purpose. These include critics and gossip, inner struggles such as fear, worry, doubt, and discouragement, health challenges, past failure, and painful delays or disappointments. His encouragement was that God blesses us in plain view, so that our opposition becomes an audience to God's goodness. He pointed to Noah, Daniel, Nehemiah, Joseph, and others, and to Jesus' resurrection, as examples of God's people serving Him in the presence of opposition.

Next he taught on the oil. In Scripture, oil signifies consecration and being set apart. Kings, priests, and prophets were anointed, and shepherds applied oil to the heads of sheep to protect them. Pastor Travis connected this to the mind, where many of us face fear, anxiety, guilt, and shame, and he described God's anointing as His calling, covering, and claiming. He recalled Samuel anointing David, still a shepherd boy, in front of his brothers, and Jesus reading from Isaiah in Luke 4 as the Anointed One, the Messiah. He noted that Saul's jealousy of David shows how God's favor can stir envy in others, and he encouraged the church to find freedom from jealousy by placing security in God alone.

Finally, he turned to "my cup overflows." He taught that God's overflow cannot be stopped by opinions or criticism, and that it is supernatural and spills onto the people around us. Using the feeding of the five thousand, he taught that God takes what we surrender, blesses it, and multiplies it. He urged the church to pursue obedience, including generous giving, and noted that love and giving go together, as seen in John 3:16. The message closed with a prayer for God's abundance and an invitation for anyone to surrender their life to Jesus Christ as a living sacrifice.
mainPoints: God does not always remove our enemies. He blesses and provides for us in front of them, so what looks like opposition becomes an audience to His goodness.
The oil in Psalm 23:5 shows that God anoints us publicly: He calls us, covers our minds and lives, and claims us as His own.
God's overflow cannot be stopped and is supernatural. It flows from surrender and obedience, as when Jesus took the loaves and fish, blessed them, and multiplied them.

versesMentioned.text: We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed.

The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters, he refreshes my soul. He guides me along the right paths for his name's sake. Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me. You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows. Surely your goodness and love will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon David.
And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing.

The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free,

As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and then led me through water that was ankle-deep. He measured off another thousand cubits and led me through water that was knee-deep. He measured off another thousand and led me through water that was up to the waist. He measured off another thousand, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough to swim in, a river that no one could cross.

Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but how far will they go among so many? Jesus said, "Have the people sit down." There was plenty of grass in that place, and they sat down (about five thousand men were there). Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. He did the same with the fish.
The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.
Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, this is your true and proper worship.

Monday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 4:8-9: "We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair."
Monday.focus: Trusting that God can use a hard season for good and for the help of others.
Monday.action: Write down one difficulty you are facing today. Beside it, write one way God has already carried you through, and one way your experience might someday encourage another person.
Monday.prayer: Lord, thank You that I am pressed but not crushed. Hold me steady in this season and use even my hardest places to help others. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Psalm 23:5: "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies."
Tuesday.focus: Reframing opposition, whether people, worries, or setbacks, as places where God can show His goodness.
Tuesday.action: Make a short list of the things that oppose your peace or purpose (for example, fear, criticism, or discouragement). Pray over each one by name and thank God that He provides for you in the middle of it. Ask Him to bless anyone on your list who has hurt you.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, I thank You that You feed and strengthen me in the presence of what opposes me. Help me to trust You rather than fear, and to respond with grace. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: 1 Samuel 16:13: "So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the Lord came powerfully upon David."
Wednesday.focus: Remembering that God has called, covered, and claimed you, especially in your thoughts.
Wednesday.action: Identify one discouraging thought that often plays in your mind. Replace it with a truth from Scripture (such as Psalm 23:5) and say it aloud three times today.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, You have set me apart and called me Your own. Cover my mind with Your peace and help me replace lies with Your truth. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: John 10:10: "I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full."
Thursday.focus: Living with gratitude for God's abundance and letting it overflow to others.
Thursday.action: Write a list of ten ways God has blessed you. Choose one blessing you can share today by encouraging someone, offering help, or saying thank you to someone who has served you.
Thursday.prayer: Jesus, thank You for the full life You give. Let Your goodness overflow in me and spill over onto the people around me. Amen.

Friday.scripture: John 6:11: "Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted."
Friday.focus: Surrendering what we have, however small, so God can bless and multiply it.
Friday.action: Name your own loaves and fish, such as your time, a skill, or a resource. Offer one of them to God today through a specific act of generosity or service. Prayerfully consider how you can give faithfully and obediently to your local church.
Friday.prayer: God, this is what I have. It may not seem like much, but I give it to You. Bless it, multiply it, and use it for Your glory. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Romans 12:1: "Offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God."
Saturday.focus: Giving all of ourselves to Jesus in love and gratitude.
Saturday.action: Set aside a few quiet minutes to surrender every area of your life to God: your heart, relationships, work, finances, and future. If you have never given your life to Jesus, tell a trusted Christian friend or a church leader and ask them to pray with you.
Saturday.prayer: Lord Jesus, You gave Your life for me, and today I give my life to You. Take my past, present, and future, and help me live for You. Amen.

title: Psalm 23 Sermon Collection: Watch Me Eat!
speaker: Pastor Travis Hearn
